question: A student claims that if two square matrices $A$ and $B$ have the same order, then $AB=BA$. Examine the claim using $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}.$$ Give mathematical justification.
explanation:
Evaluation of $AB$
$$AB=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4 & 6 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
Evaluation of $BA$
$$BA=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 \\ 1 & 5\end{bmatrix}$$
Validity of the claim
Since $AB\neq BA$, the claim is false. Even when both products are defined and have the same order, they need not be equal.

options.B: The claim is false because $AB=\begin{bmatrix}4&6\\1&3\end{bmatrix}$ while $BA=\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\1&5\end{bmatrix}$.
options.C: The claim is true because matrices of the same order always commute under multiplication.
options.D: The claim is false because $AB$ is defined but $BA$ is not defined.
